On 2023-07-28 the user asked whether I knew the Intrinsic Motivation Inventory (IMI); we discussed its structure and subscales. #imi #motivation

The IMI (Intrinsic Motivation Inventory, Ryan & Deci) has SEVEN subscales, not six: interest/enjoyment, perceived competence, effort/importance, pressure/tension, perceived choice, value/usefulness, relatedness. #imi

IMI details: 7-point Likert items (1 = not at all true, 4 = somewhat true, 7 = very true); interest/enjoyment is the only subscale that self-reports intrinsic motivation itself; pressure/tension is a negative indicator (reverse-scored). #imi

I first misstated the IMI as having six dimensions; the user corrected me ("i thought it has 7 dimension?") and I confirmed seven. Lesson: verify subscale counts before answering factual psychology questions. #imi #correction

Errors in my follow-up IMI answer needing care: relatedness means feeling connected to/cared about by others (not "related to one's values and goals"), and the "1985" attribution date for the IMI is doubtful. #imi
